sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the area in southern Calabria between the Gioia Tauro plain (to the north) and northern shoulder of the Aspromonte Mt. (to the south). This Source is a high-angle, NE-dipping, right-lateral strike-slip fault, part of the strike-slip system that dissects and advances the central and southern Calabrian arc toward SE.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) report damaging earthquakes all over the source. In particular, this region has been struck by the 16 November 1894 (Mw 6.0, Calabria Meridionale) multiple earthquake, 5 February 1783 (Mw 6.9, Calabria), and 23 October 1907 (Mw 5.9, Calabria Meridionale) events.
This Source marks a sharp tectonic and topographic shift from the the basin fill of the Gioia Tauro plain and the Dossone della Melia ridge (to the north) to the uplands of the fast uplifting Aspromonte Mt. (to the south). Despite its seismic history and the clear morphotectonic expression, this structure and its present-day role remain relatively unexplored, also due to the ever complex Calabrian geology. Although data are still unclear, we believe that this region is an actively deforming, long structure controlled by the south-easterly advancement of the Calabrian Arc toward the Ionian Sea.
Various segments of this Source have been associated with the key earthquakes of this area. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenic processes in this region, the reader may refer to the relevant Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of the Source was based on that of the mapped regional structures. Also the dip was based on geological and geometrical considerations. Rake is indicative of normal to right-lateral strike-slip faulting, based on regional geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and geometrical considerations. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.

pictures.t: Kinematic map of the Calabrian Arc
pictures.c: This map shows the strike-slip tectonics of the Calabrian Arc. The Bagnara-Bovalino source is part of the Bagnara Calabra - Bovalino Line, the southernmost major strike-slip lineament of the Calabrian Arc (from Knott and Turco [1991]).

pictures.t: Seismic profiles across the Bovalino strike-slip fault
pictures.c: These two seismic profiles show the flower structure related to the Bagnara Calabra - Bovalino strike-slip Line. In the Ionian offshore this structure shows transpressive kinematics (from Del Ben et al. [2008]).

Ghisetti [1984] describes both the Gioia Tauro Plain and the Upper Mesima basins as two graben formed by main west-dipping and secondary east-dipping faults, and points out the existence of transverse structures separating individual basins.
Schematic section of the fault systems in the general context of the active Calabrian W-dipping subduction (from Tiberti et al. [2017]).
